issue.title: [implementation-audit-fixes 03/23] Enforce cardinality under concurrency and repair canonical relation config (#82)

body:
Relay BB run pushed an update.

Pull request: #318

Tokens: 0 · Cost: $0.0000

Pushed successfully to branch `bb/relay-82-implementation-audit-fixes-03-23-enforc-thr_pq3qj62wc8`.

## Summary

This closes the final part of the relation-integrity work (#211 → #212 → #82) by enforcing cardinality under concurrency and repairing canonical relation-property config.

- **Cardinality enforcement** (`0013_relation_cardinality.sql`): a `BEFORE INSERT` trigger on `item_relations` takes a transaction-scoped `pg_advisory_xact_lock` keyed on `relation_definition_id`, then rejects a conflicting edge per the declared cardinality — `one_to_one` forbids reusing either `item_a` or `item_b`, `one_to_many` forbids `item_a` from getting a second edge, `many_to_many` is unconstrained. The advisory lock serializes concurrent inserts for the same definition so two racing transactions can't both pass the check under read-committed isolation. A new `CardinalityViolationError` (409, `cardinality_violation`) surfaces this.
- **Config repair migration** (`0014_relation_config_repair.sql`): scans every `relation_definitions` row, backfills/repairs paired properties' `targetDatabaseId` from the opposite side's `database_id`, and validates one-way properties' existing target — aborting with the offending property id on any missing/invalid/inconsistent data.
- **Real bug fixed along the way**: `Emails.attachments` was declared `one_to_many`, but that direction is structurally incompatible with "one email, many attachment files" and has no inverse to swap onto (Files' schema is locked). Corrected to `many_to_many` in `seedEmailModule.ts` — it never had a real constraint to lose, since each attachment always gets a fresh Files item.
- Added 12 new integration tests covering every cardinality, concurrency races, invalid target databases, locked-creation config completeness, and migration repair/abort behavior.

Verified: full monorepo build, migration-numbering check, dependency-boundaries check, and the complete test suite (83 unit + 415 integration + 5 e2e tests) all green, with no regressions.

Pushed successfully to the same branch: `bb/relay-82-implementation-audit-fixes-03-23-enforc-thr_pq3qj62wc8` (existing PR #318).

## Summary

Addressed the code review finding on PR #318: the `one_to_many` concurrency test relied on a 100ms `setTimeout` to sequence the two racing clients, which could invert under CI load. Replaced it with an explicit `pg_advisory_xact_lock` acquired by the winning client up front (the same lock key the trigger itself uses) — Postgres advisory locks are reentrant within one session/transaction, so the winning client's own insert still proceeds immediately, while the losing client is now guaranteed to block until the winner commits, regardless of timing. Also added a matching `one_to_one` race case (same `item_b`, different `item_a`), per the review's low-priority coverage note.

Verified: full monorepo build, migration-numbering check, dependency-boundaries check, and the complete test suite (83 unit + 416 integration + 5 e2e) all green, no regressions.

Pushed successfully to the same branch: `bb/relay-82-implementation-audit-fixes-03-23-enforc-thr_pq3qj62wc8` (existing PR #318).

## Summary

Addressed the review's blocking finding and low-priority suggestion on PR #318:

- **Semantic inversion fixed (blocking)**: the trigger had `one_to_many` backwards — it capped `item_a` to one edge, but the issue's contract puts `property_id_a`/`item_a` on the "one" side (allowed many `item_b` edges), with the uniqueness constraint landing on `item_b`. Flipped the trigger logic and its tests to match.
- **Seed data corrected accordingly**: this direction requires `property_id_a` to be the side whose own field is genuinely single-valued. Swapped source/inverse for the five paired relations where it mattered (`Tasks.project`/`Projects.tasks`, `Projects.area`/`Areas.projects` "Hub", `Projects.company`/`Companies.projects`, `Events.project`/`Projects.events`, `Folders.mailbox`/`Mailboxes.folders`). For one-directional relations that can't be swapped (`Emails.attachments`, `Files.area`, `Journal.area`, `Inbox.type`, `Inbox.journalDay`, Processing proposals' `sourceInbox`/`sourceTranscript`), corrected the declared cardinality to `many_to_many`, since none of them ever had a real single-edge invariant to enforce.
- **Trigger idempotency (low priority)**: added `DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS` before `CREATE TRIGGER` so the migration is safely re-runnable.

Verified: full monorepo build, migration-numbering check, dependency-boundaries check, and the complete test suite (83 unit + 416 integration + 5 e2e) all green.
